name: Forestpunk
tagline: Where the forest takes back what was built
description: A world lived on nature's terms, where the technology is patched, reused and half overgrown. Self-sufficiency, moss and old tools, with an undertone of resistance to anything smooth and mass-produced.

world.setting: old forest that has swallowed a farm track, fog that stays until midday
world.architecture: shacks of driftwood and corrugated iron, roofs half turf and half accident
world.interior: dried plants hanging from the ceiling, tools on the wall, everything mended at least once
world.technology: a solar panel with a crack in it, a radio that works, nothing that needs a network
world.clothes: layers of wool, waxed canvas, boots too far gone to be smart again
world.music: drone, folk melodies on worn strings, field recordings of rain
world.colours: bog black, lichen green, oxidised copper, old linen
world.everyday: mornings of firewood and coffee, days measured in light rather than clocks

name: Dark Naturalism
tagline: Nature without consolation
description: Nature seen without the idyll: wet earth, carrion, cold colours and a silence that isn't soothing. Beautiful because it is indifferent, not because it is kind.

world.setting: moorland in November, black trunks against a white sky
world.architecture: an open barn with no door, a stone wall that no longer encloses anything
world.interior: bare rooms, one window, things gathered rather than bought
world.technology: a torch, binoculars, nothing that gives off more light than it must
world.clothes: oilskin, coarse knitwear, colours that vanish against the landscape
world.music: long tones, wind in the microphone, unaccompanied singing
world.colours: bone white, peat, lichen shadow, iron grey
world.everyday: long walks with no destination, notes about weather and birds, no explanations

name: Cryptidcore
tagline: Something is standing at the treeline, looking back
description: Blurred photographs, local legends and places nobody can confirm. The pull isn't in the proof - it's that the explanation never arrives.

world.setting: gravel roads, campgrounds out of season, a sign missing a letter
world.architecture: a gas station from the seventies, a hunting cabin, a tower nobody uses now
world.interior: a map with pins in it, recording gear, newspaper clippings in a binder
world.technology: a cassette recorder, a disposable camera, a radio scanner full of hiss
world.clothes: flannel, a rucksack with too many pockets, a cap with a faded logo
world.music: banjo and synth at the same time, recordings that start too early
world.colours: pine bark, grainy grey-brown, flash white
world.everyday: driving at night, notes at three in the morning, nobody believing you

name: Cottagecore
tagline: A life slow enough to bake in
description: Country living at its most idealised: bread rising, a garden growing, work whose results you can see. Safety and handwork rather than careers and pace.

world.setting: a kitchen garden slightly too full, a fence with a rose bush over it
world.architecture: a small whitewashed house, a low door, windows with glazing bars
world.interior: copper pans, dried herbs, a tablecloth you daren't actually use
world.technology: a radio, a freezer, and preferably nothing else
world.clothes: linen layers, a cardigan, an apron that gets real use
world.music: a piano through an open window, folk songs, bees
world.colours: butter, dried lavender, apple green, unbleached linen
world.everyday: letters written by hand, Sundays with no plans, more jam than anyone needs

name: Cabincore
tagline: One cabin, no neighbours, plenty of firewood
description: Retreat into something small and warm in the middle of something large and cold. The window onto the forest matters more than the view of people.

world.setting: water lying flat in the morning, forest on every side
world.architecture: notched timber, one main room, a porch with space for two chairs and only one person
world.interior: wool blankets, a bookshelf with no system, a stove that is the centre of the room
world.technology: a gas lamp, an old record player, a phone with one bar of signal
world.clothes: a thick jumper, worn trousers, slippers that never leave the house
world.music: fingerpicked guitar, rain, wood ticking in the stove
world.colours: tar brown, wool white, deep green, ember red
world.everyday: carrying wood in, reading until it goes dark, nobody waiting on a reply

name: Naturecore
tagline: The world as it is, unfiltered
description: Plain delight in the shapes nature makes: fungi, stone, birds, tides. Less fantasy than Fairycore, less gloom than Dark Naturalism - just attention.

world.setting: a slope of lichen and heather, a shoreline of weed and shells
world.architecture: a field station, a greenhouse, something built to observe from
world.interior: pressed plants in frames, glass jars, stones on the windowsill
world.technology: binoculars, a field notebook, a camera with a macro lens
world.clothes: practical layers, earth colours, pockets for finds
world.music: acoustic, field recordings, silence between the tracks
world.colours: heather pink, lichen grey, beech green, shell white
world.everyday: walks with a book, seasons noted down, finds along the window

name: Gloomcore
tagline: Overcast, and that's fine
description: The look of grey days, hazy light and empty places. Not grief, but a pleasantly muted mood in which nothing is asked of you.

world.setting: a seafront in February, a car park in the rain, a low sky
world.architecture: concrete and glass reflecting grey, a bus shelter, an empty terminal
world.interior: few pieces of furniture, one rug, lights left off until they must go on
world.technology: headphones, a phone on low brightness
world.clothes: a rain jacket, grey jumpers, nothing asking for attention
world.music: ambient, shoegaze, singing whose words you never catch
world.colours: asphalt, haze, cold silver, pale blue
world.everyday: walking with no destination, looking out of the window a long time, leaving the phone where it is

name: Dark Academia
tagline: Knowledge as obsession
description: Old libraries, dead languages and ambitions that grow slightly too large. Beauty, discipline and a suspicion that learning costs something.

world.setting: a university quad in the rain, stairs worn down in the middle
world.architecture: neo-gothic, tall windows, corridors that carry an echo
world.interior: shelves to the ceiling, a green reading lamp, paper stacks in an order only you understand
world.technology: a typewriter, or a laptop you hide, otherwise paper
world.clothes: tweed, a wool coat, a shirt slightly too formal for the occasion
world.music: piano pieces in a minor key, choral works, the crackle of a record
world.colours: ink, dark olive, burnt umber, old paper
world.everyday: reading until two in the morning, notebooks filling faster than they are read

name: Light Academia
tagline: Learning because the world is worth understanding
description: The same love of books and buildings as Dark Academia, without the shadow. Bright reading rooms, friendship, summer and a belief that knowledge does good.

world.setting: a lawn in front of an old building, a bicycle against a wall, a summer that lasts too long
world.architecture: pale stone, classical columns, windows that let the morning in
world.interior: white walls, a wooden desk, flowers in a glass
world.technology: a laptop, but preferably a pen and decent paper
world.clothes: linen, light knitwear, a shirt with the sleeves rolled up
world.music: string quartets, early jazz, someone practising upstairs
world.colours: ivory, honey, sandstone, pale blue
world.everyday: reading outdoors, arguing too long, writing letters you actually send

name: Romantic Academia
tagline: Study as a love affair
description: The literature, the longing and the passion rather than the exam. Knowledge is something you feel as much as understand.

world.setting: an overgrown garden by a library, a bench under a tree you keep returning to
world.architecture: an old villa, a window seat big enough to sit in
world.interior: dried flowers between pages, letters in a drawer, far too many cushions
world.technology: preferably none; a phone lying face down
world.clothes: soft layers, a linen collar, a coat that is impractical and worth it
world.music: nocturnes, songs whose words you know by heart
world.colours: dried rose, wine red, yellowed paper, pale gold
world.everyday: underlining in books, writing things you never send, long evenings

name: Film Noir
tagline: The city at night, and nobody innocent
description: Hard shadow, wet asphalt and moral grey. Elegant, alone and one beat too late to save anything.

world.setting: a street where the only light comes from a sign blinking wrong
world.architecture: an office block from the forties, a stairwell, a door with frosted glass
world.interior: blind-stripes across the wall, a desk lamp, one glass
world.technology: a telephone with a cord, a car with heavy doors, nothing that stores anything
world.clothes: an overcoat, a hat, clothes that look better wet
world.music: late saxophone, double bass, rain as the rhythm section
world.colours: soot black, cigarette grey, yellow streetlight, white shirt
world.everyday: waiting, following, reaching the wrong conclusion in the right place

name: Old Web
tagline: The internet when it was somebody's home
description: Hand-coded pages, guestbooks, blinking gifs and corners of the net no algorithm showed you. Messy, personal and made by people who weren't selling you anything.

world.setting: a room with the curtains shut and a screen as the brightest thing in it
world.architecture: irrelevant - the house is a folder structure
world.interior: a CD tower, a mouse with a ball in it, a chair that doesn't match the desk
world.technology: a tower PC, the sound of a modem, pages written in a text editor
world.clothes: whatever you have on at two in the morning
world.music: MIDI versions of songs, tracks downloaded from someone you never met
world.colours: royal blue, cyan, a starfield background, white Times New Roman
world.everyday: building something nobody asked for, signing guestbooks, enjoying the mess

name: Frutiger Aero
tagline: The future was friendly, wet and made of glass
description: The optimism of 2004-2013: water droplets, glass icons, green meadows and technology promising everything would get cleaner. Nature photography as a screensaver inside a thoroughly artificial picture.

world.setting: a meadow under an impossibly blue sky, an aquarium in a reception
world.architecture: glass facades, curved forms, public buildings that look like a brochure
world.interior: white plastic, blue light, a fish in a round tank
world.technology: everything translucent, everything with a highlight, everything promising to sync
world.clothes: clean lines, technical fabric, white and turquoise
world.music: soft electronic, system tones, something that could have been an advert
world.colours: aqua, grass green, glass white, sky blue
world.everyday: everything works, everything updates, nothing breaks

name: Frutiger Eco
tagline: Technology, growing
description: Frutiger Aero with soil under its nails: bamboo, solar panels, moss on concrete and a promise that the modern can be green without becoming primitive.

world.setting: a roof garden above a busy street, green walls that actually grow
world.architecture: pale timber and glass, buildings that breathe
world.interior: plants in every corner, natural materials, little plastic
world.technology: quiet, efficient, built into something living
world.clothes: organic fabrics, soft shapes, muted green
world.music: bright electronic surfaces, birdsong in the mix
world.colours: leaf green, bamboo, chalk white, daylight
world.everyday: cycling, growing a little, believing it works out in the end

name: Vaporwave
tagline: Nostalgia for something that never existed
description: Mall music slowed into a dream, a Greek statue in pink light, ironic and sincere at once. Longing for a future that got cancelled.

world.setting: an empty mall after closing, a pool lit from below
world.architecture: an atrium with an escalator, mirrored glass, palms in pots
world.interior: a marble counter, a neon sign, a plant that may be real
world.technology: VHS, an old Mac, interfaces remembered more fondly than they were
world.clothes: a windbreaker from the eighties, sunglasses for no reason
world.music: slowed soul, mall jazz, echo on everything
world.colours: neon pink, cyan, lavender, sunset orange
world.everyday: staying up too late, missing something you cannot name

name: Y2K
tagline: The millennium was supposed to shine
description: Chrome-plated optimism around the year 2000: translucent plastic, bubble shapes, phones as jewellery and a belief that the future would be fun.

world.setting: a mall in full swing, a bus stop with an advert that glitters
world.architecture: curves, blue glass facades, everything looking like a music video
world.interior: a translucent plastic chair, an inflatable sofa, a lava lamp
world.technology: an MP3 player, a flip phone, a CD burner
world.clothes: glitter, metallics, tiny sunglasses, everything a bit too shiny
world.music: eurodance, R&B with a vocoder, ringtones
world.colours: chrome, ice blue, silver, acid pink
world.everyday: burning CDs for friends, taking joy in something entirely superficial

name: Retrofuturism
tagline: The future as the past imagined it
description: Rocket fins, flying cars and scale models of tomorrow's city. A fascination with the optimism itself, and a sadness that it never arrived.

world.setting: a fairground with a monorail that was never finished
world.architecture: domes, cantilevers, buildings that look ready to take off
world.interior: curved plastic furniture, a control panel with far too many switches
world.technology: an analogue future: valves, switches, needles that swing
world.clothes: sharp tailoring, silver detailing, uniforms for a job that doesn't exist
world.music: theremin, orchestral fanfares, early synthesiser
world.colours: rocket red, sky blue, brass, cream white
world.everyday: drawing plans for a place you will never move to

name: Atompunk
tagline: The atomic age and its shining confidence
description: America between 1945 and 1965: the space race, formica, faith in science and an optimism with a shadow of fear underneath.

world.setting: a motel with neon, a test site in the desert, a suburban street with new trees
world.architecture: googie: swept roofs, starbursts, a sign larger than the building
world.interior: formica, chrome edging, a kitchen that looks like a laboratory
world.technology: rockets, radioactive promises, appliances with a single button
world.clothes: a pastel shirt, a bow tie, a haircut with structure
world.music: exotica, space-age pop, vibraphone
world.colours: turquoise, coral, chrome, cream yellow
world.everyday: trusting engineers, planning a future with the numbers in order

name: Dieselpunk
tagline: Oil, rivets and seriousness
description: The heavy machinery of the interwar years: aircraft made of metal, engines you hear through walls, and a world built to be robust rather than comfortable.

world.setting: a dockside with cranes, an airstrip in fog, a workshop with the doors open
world.architecture: brick with iron detailing, hangars, wide concrete stairs
world.interior: steel cabinets, a map on the wall, a lamp with a metal shade
world.technology: engines you can fix with a spanner, radio contact
world.clothes: a leather jacket, work trousers, a scarf for practical reasons
world.music: brass, march rhythms, a record that crackles
world.colours: oil black, khaki, oxidised brass, concrete grey
world.everyday: keeping tools in order, work that leaves marks on your hands

name: Steampunk
tagline: The future built in brass
description: Victorian inventiveness without limits: cogs, steam, airships and devices that do far too much. Craft and excess in the same machine.

world.setting: a city of bridges and pipework, steam rising from gratings
world.architecture: iron and glass, a greenhouse on the roof, a clock tower with visible mechanism
world.interior: a workshop in the sitting room, mahogany instruments, maps and a globe
world.technology: everything mechanical, everything visible, everything slightly larger than needed
world.clothes: a waistcoat, a pocket watch, goggles on the forehead that actually get used
world.music: chamber music with machine noise, harmonium, waltzes
world.colours: brass, mahogany, bottle green, yellowed ivory
world.everyday: building something unnecessary and being made happy by it

name: Cyberpunk
tagline: High tech, low life
description: The megacity after dark: neon in rain, corporations running everything, and people making it work in the cracks. Beautiful and inhospitable at once.

world.setting: a street with no daylight, advertising larger than the buildings, always rain
world.architecture: tower upon tower, improvised extensions, concrete under fluorescent light
world.interior: a small room, many screens, cables nobody dares tidy
world.technology: modified, illegal, wired straight into you
world.clothes: technical fabric, a high collar, reflective material that hides more than it shows
world.music: industrial electronica, bass through the floor
world.colours: neon purple, toxic green, wet asphalt, magenta
world.everyday: working nights, trusting few, staying outside the system

name: Solarpunk
tagline: If we actually pulled it off
description: A future that chose community, sun and green cities over collapse. Optimistic without being naive - it takes work, and the work is the point.

world.setting: a city of canals and fruit trees, wind turbines on the horizon
world.architecture: curved timber roofs, solar panels that look like art, a shared room at the centre
world.interior: bright rooms, things made locally, tools that get lent out
world.technology: open, repairable, built to last and to be borrowed
world.clothes: colour, handmade detail, garments mended visibly
world.music: acoustic and electronic together, several people playing at once
world.colours: sun yellow, leaf green, terracotta, sky blue
world.everyday: growing, sharing, building something other people also get to use

name: Industrial
tagline: Honesty in steel and concrete
description: Beauty in what was made to work: pipework, concrete, machinery and spaces built for labour. No decoration, plenty of character.

world.setting: an industrial estate by the river, cranes against an evening sky
world.architecture: warehouse halls, steel beams left visible, tall windows in a grid
world.interior: a concrete floor, metal shelving, one good lamp over a workbench
world.technology: machines with weight, tools with a purpose
world.clothes: a work jacket, sturdy boots, nothing that can't take it
world.music: repetitive electronics, metallic sounds, echo in large rooms
world.colours: concrete grey, rust, steel blue, black
world.everyday: making things, putting tools away, respecting that something is heavy

name: Appalachian Gothic
tagline: Mountains that are keeping something
description: Isolated valleys, old families, hymns and stories that aren't told to strangers. Beautiful, warm and faintly threatening at the same time.

world.setting: a valley where the fog stays until midday, a graveyard for one family
world.architecture: a house with a wraparound porch, a leaning barn, a wooden chapel
world.interior: a quilt, a bible with notes in it, photographs of people nobody can name now
world.technology: what is needed, often forty years old and still running
world.clothes: work clothes, something kept back for Sunday, a hat that is part of the person
world.music: banjo, hymns sung without instruments, laments
world.colours: peat brown, fog grey, church white, dried blood
world.everyday: knowing everyone, saying little, keeping customs older than the house

name: Folk Horror
tagline: The village has its own rules
description: Landscape, ritual and small communities where something very old still applies. Sunlight can be more frightening than the dark.

world.setting: a field with something standing in the middle, a path through the corn, a sunset that lasts too long
world.architecture: a church with no priest, stone walls, houses turned away from the road
world.interior: a dried corn wreath, a table laid for more than are coming
world.technology: conspicuously absent
world.clothes: wool, garments for particular days, something homemade over the face
world.music: unison singing, fiddle, drums on the wrong beat
world.colours: corn yellow, blood red, moss green, chalk white
world.everyday: doing things because they have always been done

name: Adventurecore
tagline: Out, onward, further
description: Maps, tents, altitude and an urge to see what lies over the next ridge. Optimistic, practical and slightly impatient.

world.setting: high mountains, a coastal path, a camp with a view of tomorrow's walk
world.architecture: cabins you don't own, a lean-to, a lighthouse
world.interior: a pack you've repacked twice, a map folded wrong, a flask
world.technology: a compass, a head torch, a GPS on low battery
world.clothes: layers, worn boots, a jacket with a history
world.music: something with rhythm to walk to, singing round a fire
world.colours: mountain blue, burnt orange, pale stone, moss green
world.everyday: planning the next trip before this one is over

name: Lumberjack
tagline: Work, forest and coffee that's too strong
description: Physical work in the woods as an aesthetic: flannel, axes, timber and a direct, unpretentious way of taking life.

world.setting: a forest road at first light, a timber stack, a river carrying logs
world.architecture: a forestry hut, a barn, a house built from whatever was nearest
world.interior: a coffee pot, an axe on the wall, chairs that can take work clothes
world.technology: a chainsaw, a pickup, a radio with one station
world.clothes: flannel, braces, boots with steel toes
world.music: country, ballads, something to sing on the way home from work
world.colours: checked red, bark brown, spruce dark, coffee black
world.everyday: up early, working hard, saying thank you with a nod

name: Nautical
tagline: Everything stowed before you sail
description: The order and romance of seafaring: knots, brass, charts and discipline. The adventure is large, but the ship has to be tidy.

world.setting: a harbour before dawn, a lighthouse, a quay with rope coiled on it
world.architecture: a boathouse, a lighthouse, houses in white and blue against the weather
world.interior: a brass lamp, a chart under glass, everything fastened down
world.technology: a sextant, a compass, an engine that has to be maintained
world.clothes: a wool jumper, oilskins, stripes worn without irony
world.music: shanties, accordion, a foghorn
world.colours: navy blue, brass, sail white, rope
world.everyday: checking the weather, keeping order, going out anyway

name: Oceanpunk
tagline: A world of water and sail
description: Civilisations built on sea and islands: floating cities, diving bells and trade between places no chart quite covers.

world.setting: a city made of ships lashed together, coral shallows, a storm on the horizon
world.architecture: platforms, rope walkways, houses of ship's planking
world.interior: everything hanging, everything secured, glass globes with light inside
world.technology: brass diving suits, winches, navigation that is half secret
world.clothes: waterproof canvas, wide belts, colours that hold in salt
world.music: drums, part-singing, whale song in the mix
world.colours: deep sea blue, verdigris, sail white, coral
world.everyday: living by the tide, trading with strangers, trusting rope

name: Americana
tagline: The highway and everything along it
description: Diners, motels, road signs and a country seen from a car window. Nostalgia for a community that was simpler in memory than in fact.

world.setting: a straight road through flat country, a filling station with one light on
world.architecture: a chrome diner, a barn with an advert painted on it, a single-storey motel
world.interior: vinyl booths, a jukebox, a coffee cup refilled without asking
world.technology: a pickup with a tape in the player, a sign that's half lit
world.clothes: denim, a leather jacket, a cap
world.music: country, rock and roll, a radio losing its signal
world.colours: driving red, cream white, road dust, neon orange
world.everyday: driving a long way, stopping at random, talking to strangers

name: 50s Suburbia
tagline: Everything in its place, everyone in theirs
description: The postwar suburb: a cut lawn, new appliances, neighbours and an order that is safe and faintly tense.

world.setting: a street of identical houses and different mailboxes, a sprinkler running
world.architecture: a ranch house, a carport, a front garden that is purely for show
world.interior: a pastel kitchen, a three-piece suite, a television as furniture
world.technology: new white goods, a mixer, appliances owned with pride
world.clothes: a pressed shirt, pressed trousers, everything ironed
world.music: doo-wop, orchestral pop, the radio kept low
world.colours: mint green, powder pink, cream white, chrome silver
world.everyday: fixed dinners, neighbours calling round, everything exactly as last year

name: Old Hollywood
tagline: Glamour as an occupation
description: The elegance of the studio era: silhouettes, silver light, gowns and a public self carefully constructed. Beautiful, formal and deliberately unreal.

world.setting: a premiere under spotlights, a marble hotel lobby, a poolside at night
world.architecture: an art deco theatre, a Spanish-style villa, staircases made for descending
world.interior: a mirror ringed with bulbs, a chaise longue, a wardrobe larger than the bedroom
world.technology: a camera on rails, a bakelite telephone
world.clothes: bias-cut silk, black tie, gloves to the elbow
world.music: big band, a crooner, an orchestra in a film scene
world.colours: silver, champagne, deep burgundy, black and white
world.everyday: being on, always, and doing it with style

name: Art Deco
tagline: Geometry, luxury and faith in the future
description: The modern luxury of the interwar years: symmetry, expensive materials and a belief that the new should also be beautiful.

world.setting: a city street where every facade means to impress
world.architecture: stepped towers, a sunburst over the entrance, a marble lobby
world.interior: inlaid wood, mirrors in geometric panels, lamps as sculpture
world.technology: a radio cabinet as furniture, a lift with a brass panel
world.clothes: straight cuts, pearls, patterns with sharp angles
world.music: big band, a piano in a foyer
world.colours: black and gold, jade, onyx, ivory
world.everyday: surrounding yourself with things made to last and to be seen

name: Scandinavian Design
tagline: Simplicity with warmth
description: Pale wood, function and democratic beauty. The austerity is softened by materials you want to touch, and by light that is precious.

world.setting: winter light through large windows, a fjord or a treeline close by
world.architecture: clean volumes in timber, large glazing facing the light
world.interior: few good pieces, wool and ceramics, space around each thing
world.technology: discreet, well designed, put away when not in use
world.clothes: simple cuts, natural fibres, muted colours
world.music: cleanly produced, airy, faintly melancholy
world.colours: birch, chalk white, grey wool, heather
world.everyday: keeping it simple, but doing it properly

name: Maximalism
tagline: More, and with meaning
description: Rooms full of colour, pattern and collections where everything has a story. Abundance as personality, not as mess.

world.setting: a flat that is unmistakably somebody's, in a city with many layers
world.architecture: old rooms with high ceilings, ideally cornicing to hang things from
world.interior: a gallery wall, patterned wallpaper, three rugs on top of each other
world.technology: a record player, an old lamp, nothing that goes unnoticed
world.clothes: colour on colour, inherited pieces, jewellery with histories
world.music: everything, in no particular order, loud
world.colours: emerald, ochre, deep pink, gold
world.everyday: collecting, rearranging, telling people where each thing came from

name: Minimalism
tagline: Everything that needn't be there is gone
description: Fewer things, better things, and room to think. Calm through absence, and a beauty that lives in proportion rather than decoration.

world.setting: a place where little happens, and plenty of room between the things that do
world.architecture: clean planes, one good window, nothing raising its voice
world.interior: a table, a chair, one object that gets all the attention
world.technology: invisible when it isn't being used
world.clothes: the same cut in several copies, no logos
world.music: few notes, a lot of room between them
world.colours: white, grey, black, one muted accent
world.everyday: discarding more than you buy, doing one thing at a time

name: Dreamcore
tagline: Places you recognise without having been there
description: The logic of dreams as an aesthetic: empty swimming pools, corridors with no end, and nostalgia aimed at things that never happened.

world.setting: a playground at dusk with no children, a hotel corridor that repeats
world.architecture: familiar building types with the proportions wrong
world.interior: furniture in a room for no reason, wallpaper from your childhood or somebody else's
world.technology: a television left on, with no programme
world.clothes: what you were wearing when you were eleven
world.music: melodies through a wall, a cassette stretched out
world.colours: pool blue, pale pink, yellowed white, haze
world.everyday: recognising something without being able to say what

name: Weirdcore
tagline: Something is wrong with this picture
description: Low-resolution images made unsettling with text, arrows and distortion. Discomfort without threat, like a dream that almost became a nightmare.

world.setting: a place that ought to be ordinary, photographed with the wrong camera
world.architecture: a room with no door, a staircase that goes nowhere
world.interior: objects placed by someone who doesn't understand the room
world.technology: images compressed until they become another thing
world.clothes: irrelevant; the face is out of focus anyway
world.music: slowed, pitched, interrupted
world.colours: electric purple, acid green, blown-out white
world.everyday: looking at something ordinary until it stops being ordinary

name: Analog Horror
tagline: The broadcast continues after closedown
description: Horror delivered through old media: VHS noise, emergency bulletins and recordings that shouldn't exist. The fear lives in the format.

world.setting: a district with an emergency plan nobody has read
world.architecture: public buildings photographed by a security camera
world.interior: a living room with the television on and nobody on the sofa
world.technology: VHS, a test card, a voice reading instructions
world.clothes: uniforms with no agency behind them
world.music: signal tones, white noise, a melody that stops too early
world.colours: broadcast grey, warning red, phosphor green text
world.everyday: watching the recording once more to check whether you saw it wrong

name: Ghostcore
tagline: A presence that stayed behind
description: The place after the people: white sheets, old letters, rooms that still remember. More wistful and tender than frightening.

world.setting: an estate that has stood empty for two generations
world.architecture: a manor house, window casements that bang, a stair with one tread that creaks
world.interior: furniture under sheets, a clock that has stopped, a covered mirror
world.technology: nothing newer than a telephone with a cord
world.clothes: white, a thin collar, garments too light for the weather
world.music: a music box, singing far away, an organ in an empty room
world.colours: sheet white, dust grey, pale blue, yellowed linen
world.everyday: reading other people's letters, keeping a room exactly as it was

name: Fairycore
tagline: Nature with a secret people in it
description: Flowers, moss, morning light and a conviction that something small lives among the roots. Innocent, tender and slightly magical.

world.setting: a clearing with dew on it, a stream with stones that look placed
world.architecture: a house half inside a bank, a door beneath a tree
world.interior: dried flowers, glass jars, candles in every corner
world.technology: almost none, and preferably hidden behind something green
world.clothes: layers of tulle and linen, flowers in the hair, bare feet
world.music: harp, flute, singing without words
world.colours: moss, morning pink, honey gold, ivory
world.everyday: getting up early for the light, leaving something lovely for someone

name: Goblincore
tagline: The dirty, the crooked and the shiny
description: A love of mushrooms, snails, stones and things other people call ugly. Collecting, mess and delight without any need to be pretty.

world.setting: under a rotting log, a stream with shale in it, rain
world.architecture: something low, dark and snug, ideally underneath something else
world.interior: shelves of stones, shells and cutlery you didn't buy
world.technology: a torch and a magnifying glass
world.clothes: too big, muddy, with pockets full of finds
world.music: fiddle, uneven rhythm, singing with only half the words
world.colours: bog green, clay yellow, slate blue, brass shine
world.everyday: picking things up, turning stones over, caring little how it looks

name: Medievalcore
tagline: The Middle Ages as we'd like them to have been
description: The romanticised version: castles, banners, chivalry and craft without dirt under the nails. Beautiful, ceremonial and a little invented.

world.setting: a castle tower over a forest, a tournament on a plain, torches at dusk
world.architecture: spires, a gatehouse, a hall with banners along the walls
world.interior: a hearth big enough to stand in, tapestries, weapons as decoration
world.technology: irrelevant; everything that matters is done by hand
world.clothes: velvet, embroidered edging, a cloak that trails on purpose
world.music: lute and harp, fanfares, a choir in a stone hall
world.colours: deep red, gold, royal blue, stone grey
world.everyday: ceremony, craft, loyalty as an organising principle

name: Normcore
tagline: Nothing to prove
description: Deliberate ordinariness: practical clothes, familiar brands and an absence of signals. Freedom in not having to express yourself through objects.

world.setting: a perfectly ordinary street in a perfectly ordinary town, and that's fine
world.architecture: functional buildings, nothing asking for attention
world.interior: furniture that works, tidy enough, no concept
world.technology: what everyone else has, bought because it does the job
world.clothes: a jumper, jeans, trainers, no story
world.music: whatever is on, without embarrassment
world.colours: grey, navy, white, beige
world.everyday: doing ordinary things well, without making a point of it

name: Kidcore
tagline: The nineties bedroom, on purpose
description: Primary colours, stickers, toys and a deliberate reclaiming of childhood joy. Naive because that is the liberating part.

world.setting: a playground in bright plastic, a room with far too many posters
world.architecture: irrelevant; the important things happen on the floor
world.interior: stickers on every surface, collections in boxes, a patterned rug
world.technology: a handheld console, a cassette player in a loud colour
world.clothes: rainbow, stripes, far too many badges and pins
world.music: pop songs, cartoon themes, anything with a chorus
world.colours: primary red, yellow, cyan, grass green
world.everyday: doing things because they're fun, with no further justification

name: Jock
tagline: Peaked in the gym and proud of it
description: American school and college sports culture: letterman jackets, varsity numbers, locker rooms and the social gravity of the team. Wholesome, competitive and worn on the sleeve.

world.setting: a floodlit field on a Friday night, a gym that smells of floor polish
world.architecture: a brick school with a big gym wing, a stadium of aluminium stands
world.interior: a letterman jacket on the door, trophies on a shelf, a signed ball
world.technology: a stopwatch, game footage on a laptop, a scoreboard with a manual clock
world.clothes: a varsity jacket, team shorts, clean high-tops
world.music: a hype playlist in the locker room, the marching band, the crowd
world.colours: school navy, gold, bleacher grey, home red
world.everyday: practice before class, the game at the weekend, eating for the sport

name: Tacticool
tagline: Kitted out for a callout that never comes
description: Civilian gear built on a military template: plate-carrier vests, molle webbing, camo patterns and a torch on everything. Preparedness worn as style, whether or not it is ever needed.

world.setting: a range on a grey morning, a car boot organised like a kit list
world.architecture: a garage of shelving and labelled bins, a workbench under bright light
world.interior: gear on pegboard, a go-bag by the door, everything packed to a checklist
world.technology: torches, a red-dot sight, a radio scanner, a watch built like a tool
world.clothes: a plate carrier over a plain shirt, ripstop trousers, boots laced tight
world.music: not much: a podcast on the drive, comms chatter on the scanner
world.colours: coyote tan, ranger green, flat black, camo blur
world.everyday: checking the bag, dry drills, buying two of anything that matters

name: Western
tagline: Big country and a long ride
description: The visual world of the American frontier: denim and leather, worn hats, wide horizons and cattle towns. Rugged, self-reliant and heavy with myth.

world.setting: a wide plain under a huge sky, a one-street town with a rail out front
world.architecture: clapboard fronts, a porch the length of the building, a barn bigger than the house
world.interior: a wood stove, a rifle over the door, a table built to last generations
world.technology: very little: a truck, a generator, hand tools kept sharp
world.clothes: denim worn pale, a leather jacket or a duster, a hat shaped by years
world.music: country, old cowboy songs, a guitar on a porch in the evening
world.colours: dust brown, saddle tan, faded blue, dry-grass gold
world.everyday: up before light with the animals, long distances taken for granted, weather that runs the day

name: Mod
tagline: Sharp suit, clean lines, soul records
description: Early-1960s British youth style: tailored suits, parkas over the top, scooters covered in mirrors, and a devotion to soul and R&B. Neat, modern and competitive about detail.

world.setting: a city centre on a Saturday, a club night that runs till morning
world.architecture: a coffee bar with chrome fittings, a tailor upstairs, a dance hall
world.interior: a wardrobe kept sharp, a record box of soul singles, a mirror by the door
world.technology: a record player that matters, a scooter maintained to a shine
world.clothes: a slim three-button suit, desert boots, a fishtail parka for the scooter
world.music: northern soul, R&B and ska, played loud and danced to properly
world.colours: navy, red, white, black, a flash of target blue
world.everyday: pressing a suit for the weekend, hunting rare singles, riding out in a pack

name: Metalhead
tagline: Loud, fast and here for the riff
description: The heavy metal subculture: band shirts, battle jackets, long hair and a loyalty to volume. Dark imagery and technical playing over a genuinely warm community.

world.setting: a sweaty venue with a low stage, a field festival in the rain
world.architecture: a rehearsal room lined with egg boxes, a bar that has always been a metal bar
world.interior: a wall of vinyl and CDs, a stack of amps, flyers and ticket stubs pinned up
world.technology: a good amp, a guitar set up properly, a phone full of live recordings
world.clothes: a denim or leather vest heavy with patches, a black band shirt, boots
world.music: the whole point: heavy, technical, played and heard loud
world.colours: black, blood red, denim blue, chrome
world.everyday: learning the riff, driving hours to a show, defending the genre and meaning it

name: Skater
tagline: The city is only ledges and lines
description: Skateboarding and its visual world: worn shoes, filmed tricks, car parks and plazas, and a loyalty to spots most people walk straight past.

world.setting: a marble plaza that empties after six, a flat car park with good ledges
world.architecture: civic concrete read for its edges: banks, blocks, handrails, gaps
world.interior: boards stacked by the door, a snapped deck on the wall, a shelf of tapes and zines
world.technology: a phone on a small tripod, a fisheye lens, a clip trimmed to eight seconds
world.clothes: loose trousers, a tee, shoes worn through where the board grips
world.music: hip-hop and punk off a phone speaker, wheels over the joints in the pavement
world.colours: concrete grey, griptape black, faded enamel, hazard yellow
world.everyday: the same spot until the trick lands, bailing and trying again, driving across town for one ledge

name: Cassette Futurism
tagline: The future as imagined in 1979
description: A retro vision of high technology: beige plastic, CRT monitors, chunky switches, magnetic tape and monochrome readouts. The future the past expected, all wires and weight.

world.setting: a windowless control room lit by screens, a lab of grey steel cabinets
world.architecture: a bunker of poured concrete and strip lighting, rooms built around the machines
world.interior: racks of equipment with real switches, a CRT on every desk, tape reels turning
world.technology: monochrome terminals, dot-matrix printouts, a computer the size of a wardrobe
world.clothes: a technician's jumpsuit, an ID badge, sensible shoes for a long shift
world.music: analogue synth drones, tape hiss, a countdown read aloud
world.colours: beige, olive, amber readout, warning red
world.everyday: booting the system from tape, logging every reading by hand, trusting the hardware because it is heavy

name: Spacecore
tagline: Look up, and mean it
description: A love of space exploration rendered as an aesthetic: star fields, rockets, mission patches, telescopes and the deep quiet of the cosmos. Wonder backed by engineering.

world.setting: a desert launch site before dawn, a back garden with a telescope and a flask
world.architecture: a launch gantry, a domed observatory, a mission room facing one big screen
world.interior: star charts on the wall, a globe of the Moon, models of craft that really flew
world.technology: a telescope on a tracking mount, a scanner tuned to the downlink, live telemetry
world.clothes: a flight jacket with patches, a warm hat for night observing, plain and practical
world.music: ambient and choral, a countdown, radio static from very far away
world.colours: deep-space black, nebula blue, star white, booster orange
world.everyday: checking what passes overhead tonight, following every launch, learning the sky by name

name: Goth
tagline: Beauty found on the dark side of the mirror
description: The original subculture: black clothes, post-punk records and a romance with mortality that is far warmer than it looks from outside. Melancholy treated as a taste rather than a symptom.

world.setting: a city churchyard after midnight, wrought iron and wet leaves underfoot
world.architecture: Victorian terraces gone slightly to seed, pointed windows, iron railings
world.interior: heavy curtains, candles in bottles, records stacked against the skirting board
world.technology: a turntable that matters and a phone that does not
world.clothes: black on black, lace and velvet, silver at the throat and fingers
world.music: post-punk basslines, cold synths, a voice down in the chest
world.colours: ink black, oxblood, tarnished silver, deep violet
world.everyday: late nights, strong coffee, cemeteries walked for pleasure not grief

name: Trad Goth
tagline: Batcave, backcombed, and entirely unbothered
description: The 1980s root of the whole tree - crimped hair, fishnet, a club night in a basement and a drum machine doing the work. Louder and more social than the goth stereotype suggests.

world.setting: a basement club with a sticky floor and a smoke machine on its last legs
world.architecture: industrial rooms borrowed for the night, fire doors and painted brick
world.interior: flyers on every wall, a bar lit red, mirrors gone cloudy
world.technology: a drum machine, a hairdryer, and nothing else worth naming
world.clothes: fishnet over fishnet, winklepickers, hair teased into architecture
world.music: Batcave-era post-punk, drum machines, guitars soaked in chorus
world.colours: pitch black, blood red, bleached white, dust grey
world.everyday: nights that start at eleven, hairspray, friends who dress like the family you picked

name: Romantic Goth
tagline: Grief worn as brocade
description: The tender, literary end of goth - poetry, moonlight, velvet and a taste for mourning jewellery. Less club night, more ruined abbey at dusk.

world.setting: a ruined abbey at dusk with ivy taking the last of the walls
world.architecture: pointed arches, broken tracery, a chapel with no roof left
world.interior: velvet, dried roses in a jar, letters kept in ribbon
world.technology: almost none, and nothing that glows
world.clothes: long velvet, high collars, jet beads and a cameo at the throat
world.music: ethereal vocals, cello, a piano recorded in a big cold room
world.colours: midnight blue, deep plum, dried rose, tarnished gold
world.everyday: reading until the candle goes, long walks with no destination

name: Pastel Goth
tagline: Sugar on top, bats underneath
description: Lilac hair and a skull print - the dark iconography rendered in ice-cream colours. Cute and macabre held together on purpose, with no apology for either.

world.setting: a bedroom lit by a pink salt lamp with a plastic skeleton on the shelf
world.architecture: a rented room made entirely out of what got stuck to the walls
world.interior: pastel bedding, bat garlands, a shrine of enamel pins
world.technology: a ring light, a tablet for drawing, three chargers and no plan
world.clothes: pleated skirts, platform boots, a cardigan with bones embroidered on it
world.music: witch house, bubblegum pop with distortion underneath
world.colours: lilac, cotton-candy pink, mint, matte black
world.everyday: dyeing hair in the sink, drawing, posting the good photo at midnight

name: Nu-Goth
tagline: Occult minimalism with a good silhouette
description: Goth filtered through fashion editorial - clean black tailoring, a sigil worn as jewellery rather than as a statement, and a general air of expensive unease.

world.setting: a concrete gallery space with one very expensive black coat in it
world.architecture: clean lines, poured concrete, a staircase with nothing to hold
world.interior: one chair, one candle, a print nobody will explain
world.technology: a phone in a matte case and headphones that cost a month of rent
world.clothes: long black layers, sharp shoulders, a silver sigil on a chain
world.music: witch house, cold industrial, ambient with a pulse
world.colours: true black, ash, bone white, steel
world.everyday: coffee taken black, gallery openings, saying very little

name: Whimsigothic
tagline: Nineties witchy and warmer than it sounds
description: Crescent moons, celestial prints, wrought iron and lilac walls - the softer 1990s mysticism of a shop that sells crystals and incense on the same shelf.

world.setting: a house on a hill with too many wind chimes and a garden gone its own way
world.architecture: turrets, a porch with iron scrollwork, windows with coloured glass
world.interior: lilac walls, velvet, star-print throws, candles in every alcove
world.technology: a cordless phone and a stereo, nothing newer
world.clothes: long cardigans, crescent pendants, crushed velvet in plum
world.music: dream pop, Celtic harp, trip-hop somewhere in the background
world.colours: aubergine, moonlight silver, sage, dusty gold
world.everyday: tea leaves read half seriously, herbs drying, the moon noted each night

name: Southern Gothic
tagline: Heat, faith and everything left unsaid
description: Peeling porches, cicadas at dusk, family secrets and a hymn on the radio. Beauty in decay, with a moral weight that never fully lifts.

world.setting: a back road in August, heat shimmer, oaks hung with Spanish moss
world.architecture: a clapboard house with a sagging porch and paint giving up
world.interior: ceiling fan turning slowly, family photographs, a Bible nobody opens
world.technology: a transistor radio and a truck older than whoever drives it
world.clothes: cotton gone soft, a good shirt kept for church, boots with red dust on them
world.music: hymns, delta blues, a slide guitar through a small amp
world.colours: tobacco brown, kudzu green, bleached bone, rust
world.everyday: sitting out past dark, long silences, stories told the same way every time

name: Punk
tagline: Do it badly, do it yourself, do it now
description: Safety pins, stencilled slogans and three chords played too fast. An aesthetic built out of refusal, where anything polished is suspect and anything homemade is proof.

world.setting: a squat with a PA in the front room and a gig starting whenever it starts
world.architecture: condemned buildings used anyway, boarded windows, a flyer over every surface
world.interior: mattresses, a photocopier, paint straight onto the plaster
world.technology: a copier, a four-track, an amp held together with tape
world.clothes: a jacket painted by hand, tartan, boots, everything pinned and patched
world.music: three chords at speed, shouted choruses, a recording that cost nothing
world.colours: black, bleach white, warning red, cardboard brown
world.everyday: making the thing yourself, putting on the show, arguing about who sold out

name: Emo
tagline: Feeling everything, out loud, on purpose
description: Fringe over one eye, lyrics that read like diary entries, and a conviction that being unguarded is braver than being cool. Earnest to the point of embarrassment, and proud of it.

world.setting: a basement show where everyone knows the words and nobody is on a stage
world.architecture: a house with a low ceiling and a boiler in the corner
world.interior: posters over posters, a guitar leaning on the bed, lyrics on the wall
world.technology: a laptop for recording, a phone full of half-written songs
world.clothes: tight jeans, a studded belt, a band shirt worn to nothing
world.music: guitars that go quiet then loud, a voice that cracks and keeps going
world.colours: black, dark plum, red, washed-out white
world.everyday: writing at 2am, showing your friend the song, meaning it completely

name: Scene
tagline: Louder, brighter, teased higher
description: Neon streaks in black hair, stacked bracelets and a profile page coded by hand. Emo's extroverted cousin - all energy, all saturation, allergic to understatement.

world.setting: a bedroom at midnight lit by a monitor and a string of fairy lights
world.architecture: a suburban house that has no idea what is happening upstairs
world.interior: posters, plush toys, a mirror ringed with photographs
world.technology: a desktop with a hand-coded profile page and a digital camera
world.clothes: skinny jeans, layered neon, bracelets to the elbow, hair teased tall
world.music: crunkcore, pop-punk, anything with a breakdown and a synth
world.colours: hot pink, cyan, acid yellow, black
world.everyday: taking two hundred photos to get one, editing the layout again at 1am

name: Hippie
tagline: Barefoot, and meaning it
description: Handwoven, sun-bleached and communal - a rejection of the straight world in favour of music, land and each other. Idealism as a full-time practice.

world.setting: a field in summer with tents, a fire, and somebody tuning up
world.architecture: geodesic domes, a converted bus, a barn doing four jobs at once
world.interior: floor cushions, rugs over rugs, plants in every gap
world.technology: an acoustic guitar and whatever keeps the bus running
world.clothes: handwoven, embroidered, tie-dyed, mostly barefoot
world.music: folk harmonies, long jams, a tabla somewhere behind it
world.colours: turmeric, earth brown, sun-faded orange, unbleached cotton
world.everyday: cooking for everyone, growing what you eat, talking until late

name: Hipster
tagline: Everything reclaimed, nothing accidental
description: Filter coffee weighed to the gram, a vintage bicycle and an encyclopaedic interest in things just before they get popular. Craft and curation as a personality.

world.setting: a converted warehouse on a side street with a queue outside by nine
world.architecture: exposed brick, steel windows, a mezzanine nobody needed
world.interior: reclaimed wood, filament bulbs, a shelf of records and one plant
world.technology: a burr grinder, a film camera, a laptop covered in stickers
world.clothes: selvedge denim, a thrifted coat, boots resoled twice
world.music: indie folk, krautrock reissues, whatever is on the shop's turntable
world.colours: kraft brown, ink, olive, raw concrete
world.everyday: the good coffee, the long walk, knowing where everything came from

name: Rave
tagline: Four in the morning and nobody wants to leave
description: A sound system in a place that was not meant for one, strangers who are not strangers by sunrise, and a beat that does the talking. Community built at high volume.

world.setting: an empty warehouse off a ring road, found by following the bass
world.architecture: steel portal frames, roller doors, a loading bay as a chill-out room
world.interior: rigging, fog, a stack of speakers taller than anyone there
world.technology: the rig, the decks, a generator and a phone with one bar
world.clothes: whatever you can move in for six hours, reflective, oversized
world.music: acid house, breakbeat, techno that never quite lands where you expect
world.colours: UV green, deep violet, smiley yellow, black
world.everyday: sleeping through the day, living for the weekend, driving home at dawn

name: Greaser
tagline: Chrome, pomade and a bad reputation
description: Leather jackets, rolled cuffs and a car that runs because you made it run. The first teenage subculture, still trading on the same swagger.

world.setting: a garage with the door up on a warm night and an engine in pieces
world.architecture: a cinder-block workshop, a diner with a neon sign that buzzes
world.interior: a workbench, a calendar from the parts supplier, a radio on a shelf
world.technology: carburettors, a timing light, nothing with a screen
world.clothes: white tee, leather jacket, turned-up jeans, boots with a heel
world.music: rockabilly, doo-wop, early rock and roll off a jukebox
world.colours: engine black, chrome, cherry red, cream
world.everyday: working on the car, cruising nowhere in particular, being talked about

name: Rockabilly
tagline: 1955 kept alive on purpose
description: Victory rolls, upright bass and cherry prints - a whole-hearted revival that treats the 1950s as a living style rather than a costume. Sharp, social and danceable.

world.setting: a dance hall on a Saturday with a live band and a full floor
world.architecture: a mid-century hall with a sprung floor and a neon sign outside
world.interior: formica, chrome stools, a jukebox that still takes coins
world.technology: an upright bass, a valve amp, a set of hot rollers
world.clothes: circle skirts and cherry prints, pressed shirts, hair set the night before
world.music: slap bass, rockabilly, western swing, doo-wop for the slow ones
world.colours: cherry red, cream, black, warm gold
world.everyday: setting hair properly, going dancing, keeping the era running

name: Psychedelia
tagline: The pattern breathing when you look away
description: Melting letterforms, kaleidoscope colour and music built to be dissolved into. An aesthetic of perception itself coming loose.

world.setting: a room with a projector throwing oil and water onto every wall
world.architecture: a hall painted floor to ceiling by whoever had the brushes
world.interior: paisley, beanbags, a poster that is impossible to actually read
world.technology: an overhead projector, a fuzz pedal, a reel-to-reel running backwards
world.clothes: paisley, velvet flares, mirrored embroidery, round glasses
world.music: sitar drones, fuzz guitar, a mix that keeps moving ear to ear
world.colours: magenta, marigold, electric turquoise, deep violet
world.everyday: long records played whole, drawing the patterns you keep seeing

name: Soft Pastel
tagline: Blush, hearts and a deliberately gentle world
description: Cloud prints, blush stickers and pastel everything - a self-presentation that chooses sweetness as armour. Internet-native and unembarrassed by it.

world.setting: a bedroom done entirely in pink with fairy lights left on all day
world.architecture: a room in a flat, transformed by everything stuck to its walls
world.interior: cloud-print bedding, plush toys arranged by colour, a heart-shaped mirror
world.technology: a phone in a pastel case, a ring light, a tablet for editing
world.clothes: cropped cardigans, heart clips, blush worn high on the cheek
world.music: bedroom pop, hyperpop turned down, songs with a sigh in them
world.colours: blush, baby blue, lilac, whipped cream
world.everyday: decorating the room again, making things match, keeping the day gentle

name: Princesscore
tagline: The fairy tale taken entirely at face value
description: Tulle, tiaras, castles and a ballroom at the end of the story. Unironic fairy-tale fantasy with the volume turned all the way up.

gendered.description: Tulle, tiaras, castles and a ballroom at the end of the story. Unironic fantasy femininity with the volume turned all the way up.

world.setting: a ballroom lit by chandeliers with a staircase made for descending
world.architecture: turrets, arched windows, a palace built to be looked at
world.interior: gilt mirrors, silk drapes, a four-poster with too many pillows
world.technology: nothing - the fantasy does not allow it
world.clothes: tulle skirts, satin gloves, something sparkling in the hair
world.music: waltzes, harp, an orchestra swelling on cue
world.colours: lavender, gold leaf, ivory, pale blue
world.everyday: dressing up for no occasion, believing the story, arranging flowers

name: Royalcore
tagline: Portrait gallery, long corridor, family that owns a county
description: Heirloom jewellery, oil portraits and the weight of inherited rooms. Grander and colder than princesscore, with duty somewhere in the picture.

world.setting: a long gallery hung with ancestors, cold even in June
world.architecture: a stone house with a deer park and a wing nobody uses
world.interior: oil paintings, a library with a ladder, furniture older than the country
world.technology: a bell system, a telephone in the hall, nothing after that
world.clothes: tailoring made to last decades, heirloom jewellery, riding boots
world.music: chamber strings, a church organ, a piano played correctly
world.colours: navy, antique gold, oxblood, parchment
world.everyday: duty before pleasure, the estate before the self, very good manners

name: Angelcore
tagline: Feathers, marble and unbearable light
description: Cherubs, harps and white linen - religious imagery used for its beauty rather than its doctrine. Ethereal, a little mournful, faintly unsettling up close.

world.setting: a marble chapel with light coming down through high clear windows
world.architecture: vaulted ceilings, carved stone, a dome painted with clouds
world.interior: white linen, candles, statuary, dust visible in the light
world.technology: none, and the absence is the point
world.clothes: white linen, gold at the wrist, feathers, bare feet on stone
world.music: choral voices, a harp, reverb that takes four seconds to fade
world.colours: marble white, gold leaf, dove grey, pale gold
world.everyday: quiet, early light, a kind of beauty that is hard to be around

name: Twee
tagline: Small, sincere and slightly out of step
description: Cardigans, bicycles with baskets, indie pop and a fondness for the miniature. A gentle refusal to be cynical, in a world that finds that annoying.

world.setting: a market town on a Saturday with a bicycle leaned against a bakery window
world.architecture: a terraced house with a yellow door and a very small garden
world.interior: a typewriter used sincerely, jam jars, a gallery wall of postcards
world.technology: a film camera, a record player, a kettle that whistles
world.clothes: cardigans buttoned to the top, polka dots, brogues, a beret sometimes
world.music: jangly indie pop, ukulele, harmonies sung slightly flat
world.colours: mustard, sage, cream, faded red
world.everyday: baking for other people, writing notes, taking pleasure in small things

name: Cluttercore
tagline: Every surface earns its keep
description: Shelves stacked three deep, walls covered corner to corner, and comfort found in abundance rather than order. The direct answer to minimalism.

world.setting: a front room where every shelf is full and the table has a story on it
world.architecture: an old flat with alcoves, picture rails and radiators that clank
world.interior: books doubled up, postcards to the ceiling, three rugs overlapping
world.technology: a record player, a radio, a laptop lost somewhere under paper
world.clothes: layered, patterned, nothing that matches on purpose
world.music: whatever record was nearest, playing a little too loud
world.colours: amber, oxblood, moss, faded everything
world.everyday: finding things, keeping things, telling people where things came from

name: Kawaii
tagline: Cuteness as a complete worldview
description: Round shapes, mascot characters and pastel everything - a Japanese sensibility that treats charm as worth designing for, right down to the signage on a building site.

world.setting: a shopping street where every shop sign has a face on it
world.architecture: bright shopfronts stacked up a narrow street, all competing
world.interior: shelves of character goods, everything sorted by colour and size
world.technology: a phone hung with charms, a photo booth that smooths your face
world.clothes: pastel layers, character bags, hair clips in pairs
world.music: bright pop with a very high chorus, game music, jingles
world.colours: bubblegum pink, butter yellow, mint, white
world.everyday: collecting, gifting, making the small things nicer than they need to be

name: Visual Kei
tagline: The band as a total work of art
description: Androgynous costume, sculpted hair and theatrical staging - a Japanese music scene where the visual presentation carries as much weight as the songs.

world.setting: a live house with the front row pressed against the barrier
world.architecture: a basement venue with black walls and a very good lighting rig
world.interior: a dressing room of mirrors, hairspray and costume on rails
world.technology: amplification, smoke, a lighting desk run like an instrument
world.clothes: costume rather than clothing - leather, lace, buckles, sculpted hair
world.music: hard rock with classical flourishes, ballads that go enormous
world.colours: black, blood red, silver, violet
world.everyday: hours in the mirror, rehearsal, becoming somebody else on stage

name: Yami Kawaii
tagline: Cute things saying dark things
description: Pastel plush with bandages and syringes - an aesthetic that uses kawaii vocabulary to talk about illness and despair without softening either.

world.setting: a bedroom that is pink and not restful, curtains closed at midday
world.architecture: a small flat with one window and a lot of time in it
world.interior: plush toys with stitched-on frowns, pill motifs, pastel everything
world.technology: a phone, a drawing tablet, an account posting at 4am
world.clothes: pastel layers, bandage prints, a nurse cap worn as a joke that is not one
world.music: vocaloid, bedroom pop, sweet melodies with bleak words
world.colours: sickly pink, lilac, white, a red that reads as a warning
world.everyday: drawing the feeling rather than saying it, posting, being understood by strangers

name: City Pop
tagline: A bubble-era night drive that never ends
description: Neon reflections on wet tarmac, a convertible on an elevated expressway and a bassline that swings. Japan's 1980s boom years as pure atmosphere.

world.setting: an elevated expressway at 2am with the city sliding past in reflections
world.architecture: glass towers, a hotel bar on the top floor, neon down every side street
world.interior: a low-lit apartment with a city view and a very good stereo
world.technology: a cassette deck in the car, a boombox, a phone with a cord
world.clothes: a linen blazer, sunglasses after dark, gold at the wrist
world.music: AOR, funk basslines, a saxophone that arrives exactly on time
world.colours: neon pink, deep blue, chrome, amber streetlight
world.everyday: driving for the sake of it, late dinners, a city that stays awake

name: Japandi
tagline: Two kinds of restraint agreeing with each other
description: Japanese joinery and Scandinavian warmth in one room - low furniture, pale wood, hand-thrown ceramics and a great deal of empty space left alone.

world.setting: a room with one low table, a paper screen, and light moving across the floor
world.architecture: timber framing, sliding screens, a garden treated as part of the room
world.interior: pale wood, linen, one ceramic bowl that took somebody a long time
world.technology: hidden entirely, or genuinely absent
world.clothes: loose linen, wool in winter, everything in three colours
world.music: a single instrument, long silences, rain on the roof
world.colours: raw wood, oatmeal, charcoal, unbleached linen
world.everyday: tidying as a practice, tea made slowly, nothing bought in a hurry

name: Old Money
tagline: Nothing new, nothing logoed, nothing explained
description: Inherited tailoring, a sailing club and shoes resoled rather than replaced. Wealth expressed by how little it announces itself.

world.setting: a house by the water that has been in the family long enough to sag
world.architecture: a shingled house with a porch, a boathouse, nothing renovated recently
world.interior: worn rugs, sailing trophies, furniture inherited rather than chosen
world.technology: a landline in the hall and a car that is fifteen years old on purpose
world.clothes: tweed, navy blazers, tennis whites, loafers worn to the shape of the foot
world.music: a piano in the next room, jazz standards, nothing current
world.colours: navy, racing green, camel, cream
world.everyday: the same club, the same holiday, spending nothing visible

name: Mob Glamour
tagline: Fur coat, gold hoops, no apologies
description: Big fur, leopard print, heavy gold and a cigarette held like a statement. Glamour that is loud, adult and entirely uninterested in being tasteful.

world.setting: a restaurant back room where the table is always free on a Friday
world.architecture: a brownstone with a gated front and an enormous kitchen
world.interior: gilt mirrors, velvet, a display cabinet of things nobody uses
world.technology: a phone that rings constantly and a television always on
world.clothes: floor-length fur, leopard, gold layered at the neck, a red lip
world.music: Italian-American standards, disco, something with strings
world.colours: black, leopard, gold, wine red
world.everyday: family first, cooking for twenty, knowing exactly what everything costs

name: Liminal Space
tagline: A place built for people, with nobody in it
description: Empty corridors, shut-down malls and swimming pools at four in the morning. Familiar architecture drained of its purpose, which turns out to be quietly frightening.

world.setting: a shopping centre after closing with the lights still on and nobody left
world.architecture: linoleum, suspended ceilings, corridors that turn one more time
world.interior: a waiting area with chairs nobody is sitting in, a vending machine humming
world.technology: fluorescent tubes, a security camera, an escalator running empty
world.clothes: whatever you happened to have on, which is part of the feeling
world.music: room tone, a distant hum, muzak coming from an unseen speaker
world.colours: institutional beige, fluorescent white, carpet teal, exit-sign green
world.everyday: being somewhere you are not supposed to still be, and not leaving yet

name: Traumacore
tagline: Childhood imagery that no longer feels safe
description: Soft pinks and nursery motifs paired with text that undercuts them. An internet aesthetic that uses the language of innocence to describe its loss.

world.setting: a child's bedroom photographed years later with the wallpaper still up
world.architecture: a suburban house that looks completely ordinary from the road
world.interior: faded nursery wallpaper, a toy box, curtains that never got changed
world.technology: a camcorder tape nobody has watched all the way through
world.clothes: clothes from an age you are no longer, worn anyway
world.music: a lullaby slowed down until it stretches, tape hiss underneath
world.colours: nursery pink, washed lilac, cream gone yellow, faded blue
world.everyday: remembering in pieces, saying it sideways, posting at three in the morning

name: Doomer
tagline: Long coat, cold city, no particular plan
description: A grey coat, a beanie and a walk through a post-industrial city at night. Resigned rather than despairing, with a certain grim romance about it.

world.setting: a walk along a ring road at 1am with nothing open and nowhere to be
world.architecture: panel blocks, a closed petrol station, a bridge over a dual carriageway
world.interior: a small flat, one lamp, a window with condensation on it
world.technology: headphones and a phone at nine percent
world.clothes: a long grey coat, a black beanie, boots that have done this before
world.music: post-punk, ambient, one album played the whole way through
world.colours: concrete grey, sodium orange, fog white, coat black
world.everyday: walking to think, smoking in the cold, reading more than talking

name: Scenecore
tagline: 2008 rebuilt from screenshots
description: Neon gradients, pixel hearts and glitter text - the scene era reassembled by people who were too young for it, at twice the saturation.

world.setting: a profile page with an autoplaying song and a cursor trail of stars
world.architecture: none - this one lives entirely on a screen
world.interior: a bedroom with LED strips set to every colour at once
world.technology: a laptop, a drawing tablet, six tabs of GIF hosts
world.clothes: neon layers, pixel-print, hair clips, arm warmers
world.music: crunkcore, nightcore, anything pitched up and sped past comfort
world.colours: cyan, hot pink, acid yellow, black
world.everyday: editing the layout, making the GIF, staying up because it is more fun

name: Seapunk
tagline: Dolphins, chrome and a 1996 screensaver
description: Aqua gradients, 3D dolphins and Greek busts floating in cyberspace - an early-2010s internet aesthetic built from the visual junk of the dial-up era.

world.setting: a beach that only ever existed as a rendered background
world.architecture: chrome columns and a temple floating over water with no horizon
world.interior: a bedroom with an aquarium screensaver treated as decor
world.technology: early 3D software, a CRT, a CD-ROM of clip art
world.clothes: aqua tie-dye, bucket hats, prints of things that swim
world.music: chopped R&B, house with a whale sample, tape-warped synths
world.colours: aqua, chrome silver, sea green, hot pink
world.everyday: making the graphic, posting it, enjoying how cheap it all looks

name: Synthwave
tagline: Driving into a sunset that is also a grid
description: Neon grids, chrome lettering and a coastline at dusk - the 1980s as remembered by films that were never made. Nostalgia for a decade rebuilt from its soundtrack.

world.setting: a coast road at dusk with the sun setting into a grid on the horizon
world.architecture: chrome and glass towers seen from a distance, never entered
world.interior: a car interior lit red by the dashboard, and little else
world.technology: analog synthesisers, a cassette deck, a car with pop-up headlights
world.clothes: a leather jacket, aviators worn late, nothing practical
world.music: arpeggiated synths, gated drums, a solo at the four-minute mark
world.colours: neon magenta, deep purple, sunset orange, grid cyan
world.everyday: driving with no destination, night as the only setting

name: Mallsoft
tagline: Muzak in a shopping centre that closed in 2003
description: The ambient hum of consumer space, slowed and reverbed until it becomes elegiac. Retail as a haunted landscape.

world.setting: a shopping centre on a weekday with the fountain running for nobody
world.architecture: a glass atrium, planters of fake ficus, escalators crossing overhead
world.interior: tiled floors, a food court with every seat empty, a shop unit papered over
world.technology: a PA system playing to an empty concourse, a payphone still installed
world.clothes: nothing specific - you are a shopper, generically
world.music: muzak slowed to half speed, drowned in reverb
world.colours: mall beige, teal accent tile, fountain blue, brass rail
world.everyday: walking the whole loop, buying nothing, staying past closing in your head

name: Regency
tagline: Empire waist, wit, and a long walk to the folly
description: Muslin gowns, assembly rooms and pale neoclassical rooms. Restraint on the surface, with an entire social economy running underneath it.

world.setting: a country house in spring with a walk laid out to a folly on the hill
world.architecture: pale stone, symmetrical windows, a portico and a sweeping drive
world.interior: pale walls, plasterwork, a pianoforte, a writing desk by the window
world.technology: a carriage, a good pen, nothing else required
world.clothes: high-waisted muslin, tailcoats, gloves, a bonnet for outdoors
world.music: a pianoforte in the evening, country dances in the assembly rooms
world.colours: duck-egg, pale stone, straw, soft rose
world.everyday: correspondence, calls paid, long walks, everything said indirectly

name: Dark Fantasy
tagline: The old stories, with the teeth left in
description: Black forests, cursed kingdoms and heroes who lose things. Fantasy with the moral cost restored - grand, grim and genuinely dangerous.

world.setting: a forest road at dusk where the trees have been listening for a while
world.architecture: a fortress on a crag, a chapel with the roof fallen in
world.interior: a hall lit by fire, banners rotting on the walls, a long table
world.technology: iron, fire, and whatever the smith can manage
world.clothes: layered wool and leather, mail, a cloak that has kept out real weather
world.music: low drums, a bowed string, a horn from further off than expected
world.colours: pitch, moss, rust, tarnished steel
world.everyday: travelling armed, trusting nobody quickly, paying for every victory

name: Sinofuturism
tagline: Megacity at scale, lit in neon and jade
description: Vertical cities, LED calligraphy and manufacturing at a scale that stops being comprehensible. The future arriving faster than anyone planned for.

world.setting: a street at night under forty floors of signage, all of it moving
world.architecture: towers repeated to the horizon, walkways stacked four deep
world.interior: a small flat very high up, with a window that does not open
world.technology: everything, everywhere, mostly made about a mile away
world.clothes: technical fabrics, a phone as the key to the entire city
world.music: hard electronic, a pop song leaking from a shop, engines below
world.colours: jade green, neon red, concrete grey, LED white
world.everyday: speed, density, everything ordered to the door within the hour

name: Sovietwave
tagline: A future that was promised and quietly cancelled
description: Panel blocks, cosmonauts and synthesiser melodies drenched in longing. Nostalgia for an optimism that belonged to a country that no longer exists.

world.setting: a courtyard between panel blocks in February, snow going grey
world.architecture: identical concrete blocks, a playground of painted steel
world.interior: a small flat with a rug on the wall and a very warm kitchen
world.technology: a radio, a rocket on a stamp, machines built to last and to be repaired
world.clothes: a heavy coat, a fur hat, sturdy boots, nothing showy
world.music: warm analogue synths, a melody that sounds like remembering
world.colours: concrete grey, snow white, faded red, brown linoleum
world.everyday: tea in the kitchen, the same neighbours for thirty years, a future postponed

name: Midwest Emo
tagline: Twinkling guitars and a house show in a cornfield town
description: Intricate guitar lines, cracked vocals and photographs of empty streets in small American towns. Earnest, specific and quietly devastating.

world.setting: a porch in a small town in August with nothing happening for miles
world.architecture: clapboard houses on a grid, a water tower, a closed main street
world.interior: a basement with a drum kit, a bedroom with a four-track on the floor
world.technology: a cassette recorder, an old amp, a guitar with new strings rarely
world.clothes: a thrifted jacket, jeans, a shirt from a band with sixty fans
world.music: guitars in odd tunings, a voice that goes slightly out of range
world.colours: faded green, dust, cassette brown, evening blue
world.everyday: driving to the next town for a show, writing about here while still here

name: After Hours
tagline: A place you know, with everyone gone from it
description: Kenopsia: the forlorn feeling of somewhere usually full of people, found empty. A school at midnight, a park with the gates shut, a server nobody logs into any more. Melancholy, but oddly peaceful.

world.setting: a car park at two in the morning, every space empty and the lights still on
world.architecture: a school, a mall, a station - built for crowds and currently holding none
world.interior: a corridor with the strip lights humming, chairs stacked on tables
world.technology: a vending machine glowing to nobody, a clock that is slightly wrong
world.clothes: a coat pulled on over whatever you were already wearing
world.music: lo-fi, a long ambient track, the hum of a fridge two rooms away
world.colours: night black, sodium gold, window yellow, wet asphalt
world.everyday: walking at night because it is quieter, being somewhere after everyone left

name: Industrial Decay
tagline: What the machines left when they stopped
description: Abandoned factories, rust through paint, broken glass and light coming through a collapsed roof. The grandeur of very large things no longer working.

world.setting: a mill floor with the roof half gone and birch trees coming up through it
world.architecture: brick and steel built to last a century, abandoned after forty years
world.interior: rust, standing water, a control panel with every dial at zero
world.technology: machines too heavy to remove, a crane still on its rails
world.clothes: boots that can take broken glass, a jacket you do not mind tearing
world.music: drone, field recordings, metal moving somewhere out of sight
world.colours: rust orange, concrete grey, moss, shattered green glass
world.everyday: going where you probably should not, photographing it, telling nobody where

name: Soft Apocalypse
tagline: The world ends slowly, and the trees come back
